utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. We apologise for the delayed start of the hearing of today. We were informed that the witness scheduled for today is not available due to medical reasons, he's ill, but perhaps, Mr. Thayer, you have some more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President. Good morning to you and Your Honours. Good morning, General Tolimir, Mr. Gajic, good morning, everyone. The witness is very much under the weather. I met with him, and he is absolutely unable to do, I think, anything other than lie down at this point. I'm not sure what it is. It's flu or something, but he is absolutely indisposed, so he is with the doctor right now being examined. He's been sick since he got here, and it's only gotten worse unfortunately. He was okay for about a day and then went off the edge. So unfortunately we're not sure when he's going to be able to testify in the future. We'll have to look at the schedule because Mr. Ruez is on such a tight schedule because he's only available on certain days. We have been trying to schedule our witnesses so nobody pushes him further and further since he's coming from where he is currently working. I suspect that this current witness will be back sometime in April. We'll have to look at the schedule and advise all the parties. We would have scheduled him for Monday if he were healthy, but we scheduled a witness who has flown here from overseas who has somebody with him as his support person who loses work every day they're here. And they need to get on the stand, we hope, in one day, get off, and then get back to their home country. So we don't want to push that person further along either. So that's the status at the moment in terms of the witnesses. We have approximately two hours of video more that we can play today to continue along with our video review. That's where matters stand unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, the Prosecution should be aware of the time we have for all hearings. You should be prepared -- of course I see we have a problem with only sitting two days a week at the moment and that raises some problems for you by scheduling witnesses. But on the other hand we should be in a position to have a reserve witness in a case one witness can't appear for hearing and for examination. And we hope very much that we will not have this situation too often.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can tell the Court that we have begun making preparations to have some of those, what we call, gap-filler witnesses available for the future, namely, a couple of our investigators who will be available to testify on short notice about certain discrete areas that will take an hour here, half an hour there. We hope to be able to insert them as the time comes. In fact, we had one ready to go on Monday in case we ran out of time, and we'll cross that bridge when we get to it. But we share the Trial Chamber's concern certainly on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You are prepared to show us some videos. This will save some time with witnesses, future witnesses, therefore please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll turn it over to senior trial attorney McCloskey. And may I ask to be excused for the rest of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And welcome to you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're prepared to proceed where we left off. You recall we were at what we call the first Hotel Fontana meeting where they were -- General Mladic said he was calling them back later that evening. And now we have the video of that next meeting he was speaking of. And just so you know, this was material that we would have always wanted to play for you, so this is not in any way some kind of gap-filling material that you wouldn't have seen otherwise. So this is -- this is always going to be court time, and we will always endeavour to have this kind of material for you in this event. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could have a few minutes, there's some technical difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, there's been some kind of software glitch. We have to get on another software to get this out, and we're not sure, but if we could take a 15-minute break or maybe take the break now, I'm fairly confident we can get this right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we will have a break of 20 minutes. Adjourn now, and resume at quarter past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we have switched software packages, this may be -- the quality may be degraded slightly. Ms. Stewart ran this last night on -- did a dress rehearsal, and it worked fine. But, of course, now we've switched software, the quality may not be as good, but we're ready to go. We'll start now with video from Srebrenica town in the morning of the next day, the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Apparently the new software has not been calibrated correctly for the subtitling, and I apologise, Your Honours, for this. And if we could have a little more time, I think it's important to see this. Some of this you may not get to see again, though most of it there'll be a witness, if there's something of significance, that will explain who these are -- who the people are, but ... We're going to go back to one of the old original tapes which had the next Hotel Fontana meeting from the next morning of 12 July, and we'll play that right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're planning on skipping this one part because we have an updated version that's subtitles, but that's the problem with the subtitles. So we will skip ahead and go to another version. But it will be self-explanatory where we are. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is all the video that we have prepared. We will endeavour to fix the other subtitles and the other issues so we'll have more should we get gap periods. But that's all we can play for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think that's all for today. Hereto adjourn, and we will resume on Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.44 a.m.,
